about.text: Brillat-Savarin is a soft-ripened triple cream cow's milk cheese with at least 72% fat in dry matter. It has a natural, bloomy rind. It was created in 1890 as "Excelsior" or "Délice des gourmets" by the Dubuc family, near Forges-les-Eaux in Seine-Maritime. Brillat-Savarin is produced all year round, mainly in Normandy, and also in Burgundy.

how.label: add cream
how.text: Cream is added to the milk before it sets, giving at least 72% fat in the dry matter, a triple-cream cheese with a fine paste tasting of cream and fresh butter. The long, cool lactic set gives a mildly acid taste, and only the 'affiné' version grows a white bloomy rind.

steps.note: Cow's cream, before the milk sets.
Set mostly lactic, with calf rennet of up to 20 ml per 100 L.
At pH 4.9 or less, drained by gravity without pressing, as cylinders of 100–250 g or 500 g and more.
Only the affiné version is ripened, for at least 5 d (small) or 8 d (large), while the fresh one is sold from day 3.
